claims.statement: Budgeted graph repair can reduce downstream decision loss relative to no repair within the frozen synthetic contract.

research_d.unit: 200 corruption draws conditional on one DRF DGP and one training frame

claims.limitation: Research D is semisynthetic and does not establish physical manufacturing effects.

claims.statement: M4 uses fewer atomic edits on average in the reported comparisons.
claims.limitation: Edit count is not labor, time, monetary cost, or safety cost.

claims.statement: Path availability and estimated effect direction help explain observed decision differences.
claims.evidence: Original-ledger post-hoc analysis; 49 of 55 held-out S0 regret-positive cases lacked an X-to-Y path; 5 of 6 M4-winning action disagreements restored a path and one retained an existing path but selected a different action direction.
claims.limitation: Exploratory post-hoc mechanism analysis, not confirmatory mediation.

claims.statement: M4 is always superior to Full Greedy.
claims.counterexamples: Full Greedy wins some Research C cases; Research D M4 loss exceeds Full Greedy by 0.00122956.

claims.statement: Graph-based repair generally outperforms graph-free regression.
claims.evidence: Research D graph-free association baseline loss equals Full Greedy loss at the reported precision.

claims.statement: The method has been validated on physical manufacturing interventions or is deployment-ready.
claims.evidence: No physical intervention validation was performed.
